Traditional sparse retrieval (BM25) relies on exact lexical matching — it fails when the query says “car” but the document says “automobile.” Dense retrieval (DPR) captures semantics but loses interpretability, requires GPU at query time, and produces large indexes. blocks.originalExcerpt: Chunking is the process of splitting documents into segments that are (1) small enough to fit in an embedding model’s context window, (2) semantically coherent, and (3) contain enough context to be useful when retrieved in isolation.

RAG的一个实际瓶颈是解码空档:被检索到LLM背景的段落往往长而鲜有关联，夸大了时间到第一脚趾(TTFT)和KV-cache内存。 REFRAG [220] 观察到，由于检索的通道是独立来源的(通过复位时的多样性或减位)，它们的注意力模式是块-对角-几乎交叉通道的注意力接近零。这种拼接表示，在解码时，大多数计算都超越RAG上下文是不必要的。
blocks.originalExcerpt: A practical bottleneck of RAG is decoding latency: the retrieved passages concatenated into the LLM context are often long yet sparsely relevant, inflating time-to-first-token (TTFT) and KV-cache memory. REFRAG [220] observes that because retrieved passages are independently sourced (via diversity or deduplication during re-ranking), their attention patterns...

blocks.text: 压缩- 感知- 扩展框架。 REFRAG 通过三阶段解码策略来利用这个结构 :
blocks.originalExcerpt: Compress–Sense–Expand Framework. REFRAG exploits this structure via a three-phase decoding strategy:

blocks.text: 1. 压缩:用紧凑摘要取代已检索段落的 KV 全文说明
blocks.originalExcerpt: 1. Compress: Replace full KV representations of retrieved passages with compact summaries

blocks.text: (例如，每个通过块的均值集合键/值)，大幅降低内存。
blocks.originalExcerpt: (e.g., mean-pooled keys/values per passage block), drastically reducing memory.

blocks.text: 2. 理智:在每个解码步骤上，使用轻量级的注意力，而不是压缩的表示方式
blocks.originalExcerpt: 2. Sense: At each decoding step, use lightweight attention over the compressed representations

blocks.text: 以识别哪些通道块与当前符号相关。
blocks.originalExcerpt: to identify which passage blocks are relevant to the current token.

blocks.text: 3. 扩展: 仅为选定的块重建完整的 KV 条目， 进行精确的注意
blocks.originalExcerpt: 3. Expand: Reconstruct full KV entries only for the selected blocks, performing exact attention

blocks.text: 以少数的活跃的集合盟誓，

前面的章节介绍了个别的部件——路线、检索、评估——一个完整的AgentRAG系统将这些部件作为状态节点的图来编织，控制流动取决于中间结果。以下执行使用 LangGraph 将四个节点连接成环线:
blocks.originalExcerpt: The previous sections introduced individual components—routing, retrieval, evaluation. A full agentic RAG system orchestrates these as a graph of stateful nodes, where control flow depends on intermediate results. The implementation below uses LangGraph to wire four nodes into a loop:

blocks.text: 1. 计划:将用户查询分解为sub-query(每个信息需要一个)。
blocks.originalExcerpt: 1. Plan: Decompose the user query into sub-queries (one per information need).

blocks.text: 2. 检索:将每个sub-query划到适当的来源并获取文档。
blocks.originalExcerpt: 2. Retrieve: Route each sub-query to the appropriate source and fetch documents.

blocks.text: 3. 评估:判断累积上下文是否足以回答最初的询问。
blocks.originalExcerpt: 3. Evaluate: Judge whether the accumulated context is sufficient to answer the original query.

blocks.text: 4. 生成:用检索到的文档引用来合成最后的答案。
blocks.originalExcerpt: 4. Generate: Synthesize a final answer with citations from the retrieved documents.

上面的AgentRAG方法依赖于即时工程的管弦——Agent的搜索行为由指令控制，而不是通过训练来学习。搜索-R1[170]采取了一个根本不同的方法:它通过强化学习来训练LLM，学习何时，什么，以及作为推理过程的一部分搜索多少次。
blocks.originalExcerpt: The agentic RAG approaches above rely on prompt-engineered orchestration — the agent’s search behavior is controlled by instructions, not learned through training. Search-R1 [170] takes a fundamentally different approach: it trains the LLM via reinforcement learning to learn when, what, and how many times to search as part of its reasoning process.

blocks.text: Core Idea。 Search-R1通过将搜索引擎查询作为RL训练环内的行动来扩展DeepSeek-R1 [72] 推理框架。在思维链生成过程中，模型可以发出特殊符号<search>query</search>，触发从搜索引擎进行实时检索。检索的结果被注入推理上下文，模型继续生成。
blocks.originalExcerpt: Core Idea. Search-R1 extends the DeepSeek-R1 [72] reasoning framework by treating search engine queries as actions within the RL training loop. During chain-of-thought generation, the model can emit special tokens <search>query</search> that trigger real-time retrieval from a search engine. The retrieved results are injected back into the reasoning context, ...
